newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Liberte has no comment on bankruptcy report.
newsitem.headline: Air Liberte has no comment on bankruptcy report.

text.p: Privately owned French carrier Air Liberte declined to comment on a radio report that it had filed for insolvency protection on Thursday with a court in Creteil.
A spokeswoman said she could not confirm the report, which cited court sources, but said Air Liberte Chairman Lotfi Belhassine was hosting a news conference at 1600 GMT.
Radio France Info said the company had presented a recovery plan entailing 250 job cuts and a focus on short and medium routes during a six-month creditor protection period.
French newspapers report Air Liberte will show a loss for the year to the end of October of around 600 million francs.
It lost 160 million francs in the first half of 1995/96.

The owners of the airline are Banque Rivaud, with 33 percent, Banque Indosuez, with 13 percent, International Leasing Finance Corp, a unit of U.S. American International Group, with 12 percent, Euralair, with 10 percent, Club Mediterranee, with 8.5 percent, Lyonnaise de Banque with 6.2 percent, and Eiffage, with five percent.
Belhassine owns six percent and other investors hold a combined 6.3 percent.
Belhassine has blamed the airline's woes on a price war and preferential treatment given to state-owned Air France by Paris airport authorities.
